clue.text: Day in hole at the bottom of Auld Reekie?

indicators.note: in places the abbreviated weekday inside the vulgar word for an anus

parts.note: arse is vulgar British slang for the backside or its hole
Thurs is the short form of Thursday
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crude remark about some low spot in Edinburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: Auld Reekie is a nickname for Edinburgh; Arthur's Seat is the big hill in the middle of the city. Seat means bottom, so the hill is playfully the city's backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat is a bottom, and this hill is Edinburgh's famous seat, so the question mark flags the pun.

clue.text: Star burying one's treasure — he has the money

indicators.note: burying means one piece is sunk inside the star's name

parts.note: Altair is the brightest star in the constellation Aquila
one is I, and one's is short for one is, giving I plus S
a treasure is a beloved person, a darling

explanation.surface: A celebrity hides their riches, and somebody else holds the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue dates from 2009, when this man was the UK's Chancellor of the Exchequer, the minister in charge of the nation's finances.
explanation.definitionFit: As Chancellor of the Exchequer he was the politician holding the Treasury purse strings, a witty description.

clue.text: Bone found in hospital, useful

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bone discovered in a hospital turns out to be handy.
explanation.definitionFit: The talus is the ankle bone, which links the leg to the foot.

clue.text: Experience unconscious energy

parts.note: someone under anaesthetic is unconscious, so under means out cold
go means energy or drive, as in full of go

explanation.surface: Feeling a burst of vitality without being aware of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To experience something, such as surgery or a change, is to go through it, a synonym.

clue.text: Mammoth starter unfortunately brought up is sausages

indicators.note: brought up in a down entry means the pieces read from the bottom upwards
starter means the first letter of the word Mammoth

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge breakfast went badly and came back up as sausages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns M plus the sigh of regret together, giving SALAM; the reversal suits a down entry, read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Salamis are spicy cured sausages from Italy, plural to match the clue.

clue.text: Fantasy with English piano is carried by fiddle

indicators.note: carried by means the pieces are held within the swindle word

parts.note: a fiddle is a swindle, a scam
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A whimsical piece for piano is accompanied by a violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' looks like the violin in a musical scene, but here it is the dishonest kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapism is retreat into fantasy and daydreams away from reality, a near synonym.

clue.text: Going to pot, tries tea with hot milk — what an improvement!

indicators.note: going to pot means falling apart, so the letters that follow are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone samples tea with hot milk while everything is falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of approval when something gets better, matching the clue's exclamation.

clue.text: Musical tune finds speed with a runner, whatever it is

parts.note: to zip is to go fast, so zip means speed
a runner in crosswords is a river; the Dee is a river in Scotland and Wales
a doodah is a thingummy, a word for an object whose name escapes you

explanation.surface: A song gains pace with a sprinter, whatever that may be.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Oscar-winning song from the Disney film Song of the South, so a musical tune.

clue.text: Payback time here?

parts.note: doing time as a way of paying back what is owed: a jail for people who could not settle up

explanation.definitionFit: A jail of former times held those who failed to repay money owed, so time was served for money.

clue.text: Cold centre of quiche in shop returned, as frozen

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the reversed shop
returned means the shop word is read backwards

parts.note: a deli is a shop selling cooked meats and cheeses
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle two letters of quiche

explanation.surface: A chilled quiche was taken back to the shop because it was frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the shop word into ILED, and the cold letter plus the quiche's middle go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hung with icicles is frozen solid, a near synonym.

clue.text: Didn't have the figure, say, to prepare to feed baby

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken and heard as one word

parts.note: lacked eight: did not have the number 8

explanation.surface: A woman who lost her figure gets ready to nurse her infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' looks like body shape after pregnancy; it is a number, eight.
explanation.definitionFit: To lactate is to produce milk, which a mother does to make ready to nurse.

clue.text: Doctor ruminates, seeking treatment for disease

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of the next word are altered

explanation.surface: A physician ponders while looking for a cure.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiserum is blood serum containing antibodies, given as a treatment against infections.

clue.text: Kitty pinching is put back, or put forward

indicators.note: pinching means the pot word holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of money, a pot

indicators.note: put back means the little word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cat steals something that is returned, or offered up.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit an idea is to propose it, put it forward for discussion.

clue.text: Bad to be in recession

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to live is to be alive, to exist

explanation.surface: Economic hard times are a bad thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil means wicked or very bad, a synonym.

clue.text: Person fitting animal to its anagram?

definitions.text: Person fitting animal to its anagram?

parts.words: Person fitting animal to its anagram?
parts.note: a farrier joins a creature to footwear, and the word for the footwear-fitter rearranges the creature's name

explanation.definitionFit: A farrier who nails iron plates onto a mount's hooves; the second half rearranges the first.

clue.text: Cutting technique for old jumper?

parts.note: a tool for cutting, and also an old-fashioned high-jump style where the legs cross like blades

explanation.definitionFit: These are a cutting tool, and also the name of an outdated high-jump style used by athletes.

clue.text: Lecturer maintaining order without a single commitment

indicators.note: maintaining means the lecturer holds the following pieces inside

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the order wraps around the a

parts.note: an edict is an official order or decree
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit

explanation.surface: A tutor keeping order without a single act of commitment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: EDICT goes round A to give EDICAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Dedication means commitment to a cause or task, a synonym.

clue.text: River swallowed up fine material

parts.note: the Taff is a river in Wales, flowing through Cardiff

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: swallowed means ate

explanation.surface: A river engulfed some delicate fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous fabric, often silk, used for fine dresses.

clue.text: Withdraw head from very fertile bird

indicators.note: withdraw head from means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: most rich means extremely fertile, as of soil

explanation.surface: Pulling the head out of the sand on very rich land.
explanation.walkthrough: MOST RICH loses its first letter, M.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a large flightless bird of Africa.

clue.text: Man put on record — one from the '60s

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A man plays a record from the sixties.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the Beatles' 1965 album and film, which was a record from that decade.
explanation.definitionFit: Help! is the Beatles' 1965 album and film, one item from that decade.

clue.text: Lessening of growth on yellow flower

indicators.note: on in an across entry means the shortened growth is placed after the yellow

parts.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry

indicators.note: lessening of means the growth word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a rise is an increase, growth

explanation.surface: Reduced growth seen on a yellow bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Yellow as OR is the heraldic colour gold, a convention worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is a kind of iris, the flower whose root gives a fragrance.

clue.text: Cook cut it fine, serving Italian dish

indicators.note: to cook is to falsify or alter, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A chef leaves things late serving pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Fettucini is a ribbon pasta, served as an Italian dish.

clue.text: American state university raised the standard

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means the pieces read upwards

parts.note: LA is Louisiana, a US state

explanation.surface: An American state college has lifted its standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns LA plus U to give UAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual is the normal, standard thing, a synonym.

clue.text: I sit on Bill, fatty

indicators.note: on in an across entry means placed after the bill

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a bill
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: Someone sits on a bill, overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose means relating to fat, as in adipose tissue.

clue.text: Routine surgery within the womb

indicators.note: surgery is an operation, so the letters are operated on and rearranged

explanation.surface: A standard operation inside the uterus.
explanation.definitionFit: In utero is Latin for in the uterus, so within the womb.

clue.text: Short musical lines break in blow for composer

indicators.note: in means the two pieces sit within the blow word

parts.note: a gust is a blow of wind

indicators.note: short means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a stave is the set of five lines on which music is written
hol is short for holiday, a break

explanation.surface: Brief musical lines interrupt a gust for a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the last letter of the stave; 'break' is clipped to its usual abbreviation, as in going on hols, the British word for holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: The English composer of The Planets, an example of a composer.
